#  13314 - Instrumental Analysis and Physical Chemistry Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **13314**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Instrumental Analysis and Physical Chemistry**  |  
|  Instrumentelle Analytik und physikalische Chemie   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 2 - Environment and Natural Sciences   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Schmid, Reiner 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every summer semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  |  **Part 1: Introduction to modern instrumental analytical techniques** The student gets an overview of the most important instrumental analytical methods and their fields of application. After completing the module, the student is able
  * to understand the physical relationships that provide the theoretical foundations of instrumental analysis.
  * to evaluate instrumental analytical methods with respect to their performance and their scope of application.
  * to interpret/evaluate spectroscopic and chromatographic data.
  * to derive structures of simple organic compounds from spectroscopic data.

**Part 2: Introduction to Physical Chemistry** The student gets an overview of the most important concepts of classical physical chemistry. The student achieves:
  * the ability, to connect different subdisciplines of physical chemistry, due to their understanding of important common concepts.
  * an overview which could be adapted to other fields.
  * the ability, to solve simple problems out of the respective topics.
  * interdisciplinary knowledge, due to inclusion of practical examples from different technological areas.

 |  
| Contents:  |  **Part 1:** Introduction to Instrumental Analysis
  * Performance characteristics of different methods
  * Errors in Analytical Chemistry

Separation Techniques
  * Fundamentals of Chromatography
  * Gas Chromatography (GC)
  * High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC)
  * Thin-Layer Chromatography (DC)
  * Size-Exclusion Chromatography (SEC)

Mass-Spectrometry
  * General
  * Ionisation Methods
  * Mass-Analyzers and Detectors
  * Interpretation of Mass-Spectra

Spectroscopic Methods
  * Characteristics of Electromagnetic Radiation
  * Introduction to Spectroscopy
  * Infrared (MIR) – Absorption-Spectroscopy
  * Ultraviolet/visible (UV/VIS) – Absorption-Spectroscopy
  * Fluorescence; Phosphorescence and Chemoluminescence
  * Atomic Absorption (AAS) / Atomic Emission (AES)

**Part 2:** Thermodynamics
  * The properties of gases, ideal gas equation, van der Waals equation
  * 1st law of thermodynamics, internal energy, work and heat, enthalpy, heat capacity, Carnot cycle, Joule Thomson effect, liquefaction of gases
  * thermochemistry, Hess’s law, temperature dependence of reaction enthalpy (Kirchhoff’s law), calorimetry
  * 2nd law, entropy, heat engines, Gibbs energy, chemical potential

Physical transformations of pure substances 
  * Phase diagrams, phase boundaries, Clausius-Clapeyron equation

Properties of simple mixtures
  * Chemical potential of liquids, Raoult’s law, Henry’s law, Colligative properties, Phase diagram of mixtures

Chemical equilibrium 
  * Gibbs energy minimum, relation of Gibbs energy and the equilibrium constant

Chemical kinetics
  * Rates of reactions, integrated rate laws, first-order reactions, half-lives, radiocarbon dating, temperature dependence of reaction rates (Arrhenius equation), relation of equilibrium constant and the rates of reaction
